chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Joe's opinion of Mutt Carey's trumpet playing
summary: Joe thinks Mutt was one of the weakest New Orleans trumpeters, with a thin tone but good wah-wah mute work.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Did Mutt ever copy anybody's solos that you knew of when you were with him?
No. To me, Mutt was one of the weakest of all the Hew Orleans trumpet players, to tell you the truth.
Well, talking to various musicians, I've heard that he wasn't musically that...
He was a good man with a wah-wah mute or something like that. Mutt didn't have any chops -- any
power; that's what I'm saying. And he had a very thin tone.
It's a funny thing. That tone is the most recognizable thing about him. It sounds... I've heard it described as like a billy-goat...

And I've heard it described as a laser-beam that would cut through metal. I think you either liked his tone or didn't like his tone, you know. I personally like Mutt's playing a whole lot. But many musicians have said the same thing that you do, Mutt was the weakest one in the band.
